title: Phasebound Admittance Curator for Canary Releases
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: current canary tooling expresses only static step schedules (0%, 5%, 25%, 100%) and simple metric gates. That surface makes it hard to: 1) express cohort-aware admission windows, 2) gracefully throttle introduction when backend resource usage/latency drift, and 3) tie rollback sensitivity to per-customer SLOs.

Goal: ship an operator (Phasebound Admittance Curator) that lets platform users declare flexible 'phases' with local guards, cohort routing hints, and adaptive backoff curves. The operator should: 1) allow phase definitions with targeted traffic splits (by cohort or globally), 2) evaluate sliding-window SLO contracts and degradation trends rather than point-in-time thresholds, 3) optionally run shadow probes and golden-traffic validators before opening exposure, and 4) trigger automatic rollback or damped-growth when risk signals exceed configurable budgets.

Outcomes: reduce noisy rollouts, provide safer defaults for multi-tenant workloads, and give SREs/Platform teams per-release observability and deterministic rollback behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Users can define a canary rollout using a phasebound DSL with at least: phases (name, duration, target_split), gates (metric, operator, window), and backoff policy (linear|exponential) and policy weight.
Runtime enforces phase duration and gate evaluations, and will not advance phases until gates pass or backoff limit reached.
Automatic rollback triggers when configured composite gate hits the failure budget (e.g., sustained latency > p95 target for 2 consecutive windows).
Console UX shows phase-by-phase live split, recent gate evaluations, and a one-click abort/rollback action for operators.
End-to-end tests simulate cohort traffic and validate the operator stops advancement and rolls back on injected latency spikes.
technical_notes:
Design summary: a lightweight policy engine that compiles a phasebound DSL into a deterministic evaluation graph. Each phase exposes: 
- target_split: percentage or cohort selector (e.g., header:user-cohort=beta)
- probes: optional shadow request templates and expected invariants
- gates: array of (metric, comparator, threshold, window_seconds, required_consecutive_windows)
- backoff: { strategy, max_retries, cooldown }

Runtime integration notes: the router will query the curator for routing decisions (sync call with TTL cache) and fallback to a legacy traffic-split table if curator unavailable. Gate evaluation is implemented in the control plane using sliding-window aggregations emitted by the runtime tracing hooks (Console already emits token-level latency and error counters). We will reuse the existing time-series store (metrics-TSdb) and add pre-aggregated windows for common buckets (30s/2m/10m).

Policy determinism: to avoid split flapping under clock skew, the curator uses vector clocks based on phase IDs and monotonic counters. Decisions are idempotent and recorded to the audit log to allow post-mortem reconstruction.

Config DSL example (informational):
phases:
  - name: shadow-probe
    duration: 300
    target_split: 0%
    probes:
      - template: "{prompt: \"sanity-check small prompt\"}"
    gates:
      - metric: probe_invariant_failures
        operator: <=
        threshold: 0
        window_seconds: 60
        required_consecutive_windows: 3
  - name: cohort-early
    duration: 3600
    target_split: "cohort:beta=5%"
    gates:
      - metric: p95_latency
        operator: <=
        threshold_ms: 350
        window_seconds: 120
        required_consecutive_windows: 2
    backoff:
      strategy: exponential
      max_retries: 4
      cooldown: 300
rollout_plan:
Phase 0: implement control-plane policy engine and DSL parsing (iteration 1). Phase 1: integrate gate evaluations with metric windows and add audit logs. Phase 2: runtime routing hook and TTL cache. Phase 3: Console integration with charts and manual override. Phase 4: end-to-end QA and canary the operator on an internal service.

Milestones: 
- Week 1-2: DSL + evaluation graph + unit tests.
- Week 3: metrics windows + integration tests with metrics-TSdb.
- Week 4: runtime routing integration + TTL fallback.
- Week 5: Console UI + docs + internal canary.

Rollout strategy: feature-flagged behind 'phasebound-rollouts' and gated to Dedicated tenants first, then Hosted experiment cohorts.
testing_plan: Unit tests for DSL compiler covering edge cases (overlapping cohorts, inconsistent percentages, invalid gates).
Integration test that uses a synthetic metrics emitter to verify backoff and rollback behavior under injected latency trends.
Chaos test: inject intermittent curator unavailability and ensure router TTL fallback preserves previous safe splits and triggers no unsafe advancement.
E2E smoke on staging with an internal model: shadow probe -> 5% cohort -> incremental advance to 25% with simulated SLO regressions causing rollback.
review_feedback: PM (Jared Simmons): prefer conservative defaults for backoff; default backoff = exponential with max_retries=3.
SRE (Liang Wu): require at-least-one golden invariant for releases touching production embeddings; otherwise block promotion.
Design (Ruth Gomez): Console needs a compact timeline view that highlights gate failures and suggested operator actions.
Security (Amelia Rowe): add an audit-only mode that records decisions without mutating routing for first two weeks of rollout.
